$comment: MIGRATION VERSION RESERVATION REGISTRY (GOV-H, 2026-11-01).
A migration version is claimed REPOSITORY-WIDE, not per branch. The
uniqueness rule in scripts/check-migration-quality.js can only compare a new
migration with the files in the CURRENT checkout, so it is structurally blind
to a version claimed by a sibling branch and completely blind to one that
exists only as an uncommitted file in another worktree.
That blindness is not theoretical. THREE branches each claimed 20270110000000:
0d87637c  20270110000000_pi_prospect_problem_actor_fk_removal.sql  (PPO, PR #364, MERGED)
9f710167  20270110000000_canonical_leads_users_client_privileges_revoked.sql  (SEC-A)
9f359da0  20270110000000_media_h3_storage_quarantine_policies.sql  (media H-3)
At 9f710167 the tree held exactly ONE file at that version, so the gate
passed and the collision was invisible. It was resolved the right way: the
UNMERGED migrations were renumbered (SEC-A..SEC-B to 20270111000000-03, media
H-3 to 20270116000000) and the MERGED one kept its version. A migration
already applied to production is never renamed.
This registry is the durable half of the fix: a claim recorded here travels
with the repository, so any branch that rebases sees it and a second claim on
the same version fails the gate. The pre-integration half is
'node scripts/check-migration-quality.js --scan-refs', which enumerates every
branch tip AND every registered worktree's uncommitted on-disk files.
STATUS VALUES
occupied_elsewhere - the version is taken by work not in this checkout
(another branch, or an uncommitted file in a worktree).
A new migration using it FAILS the gate.
reserved           - allocated to a named track for a named slug. A file at
this version must use that slug.
merged             - the version is on origin/main. Recorded so it can never
be re-claimed or renumbered.
Remove an entry only when the version is on origin/main (then record it as
'merged') or the work was abandoned and the files deleted everywhere.
